headline: Wide refining margins drive a blowout quarter
summary_short: Valero's Q2 2026 revenue rose to $44.48B (+48.8% y/y, +37.4% q/q) as refining margin per barrel roughly doubled to $23.62 from $12.35 y/y, driving diluted EPS to $12.62 (+453.5% y/y) and net income to $3.72B (+421.0% y/y).
summary_long: Refining operating income rose to $4.47B from $1.266B as USGC crack spreads widened sharply (ULS diesel-less-Brent $43.52 vs $14.79 y/y), lifting margin per barrel to $23.62 from $12.35. Renewable Diesel swung to $717M operating income (from a $79M loss) as margin per gallon rose to $2.52 from $0.22 on higher RIN prices; Ethanol operating income rose to $318M from $54M. Net income reached $3.72B ($12.62 diluted EPS), aided by a lower diluted share count (294M vs 312M). Cash rose to $7.87B from $4.54B y/y; total debt was $9.1B. Valero returned $2.6B to shareholders and declared a $1.20/share dividend. No forward guidance was issued; the $230M St. Charles FCC project remains on track for Q3 2026 startup.

drivers.explanation: Refining external revenue rose to $42.3B from $28.3B on far wider realized crack spreads (refining margin per barrel $23.62 vs $12.35 y/y); Renewable Diesel and Ethanol external revenue were roughly flat to modestly higher.

Refining segment operating income rose to $4.47B from $1.266B on the margin widening above; Renewable Diesel swung to $717M from a $79M loss as margin/gallon rose to $2.52 from $0.22 on higher RIN prices ($2.12 vs $1.09); Ethanol rose to $318M from $54M.
Tracks the same refining-margin and Renewable Diesel/Ethanol swing described for operating income, plus $116M of other income, net, which operating income excludes.
Same segment margin drivers as operating income, before $723M of depreciation and amortization (down slightly from $786M y/y as Benicia Refinery D&A shifted to a shortened salvage-value schedule).
Follows the operating-income improvement described above; the effective tax rate was 21% for the quarter, and the year-ago quarter carried no offsetting one-off items of comparable size.
Net income growth was amplified by a lower diluted share count (294M vs 312M y/y) from ongoing buybacks funded within the $2.6B of quarterly stockholder returns.

Net cash from operating activities was $5.6B (including a $706M working-capital benefit), funding $350M of capital investment and $2.6B of stockholder returns while cash still rose to $7.87B from $4.54B a year earlier.

CEO Lane Riggs attributed the quarter to "excellent operations and commercial execution across all three of our business segments"; no forward guidance was issued, and the $230M St. Charles FCC optimization project remains on track for Q3 2026 startup.
